comparison.objective: Hold a shelf against an irregular wall and trace its profile with a pencil compass; the candidate instead adjusts and locks a gripper stop before testing its retained opening.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1871 requires sustained surface-guided compass motion, simultaneous shelf stabilization, tool orientation, and continuous precision marking. The candidate requires concentric two-tool engagement, coordinated countertorque that prevents screw drift, wrench regrasping, and subsequent lever actuation.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1871 grades a continuous edge-to-edge curved line at 14 stations, profile bend, compass placement, shelf/tool stillness, clearance, and loss events. The candidate grades opening-angle tolerance, locknut seating and retention, repeated-cycle return, drift, and released clearance. All available versions specify the relevant numeric rubric; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: Although both use two hands and require stabilizing one element while manipulating a tool, tracing a surface profile into a continuous accurate mark is a different tested ability from counterholding a coupled adjustment during locknut tightening and proving retained mechanical function.
